question.problem: Given that $f(x)=4\cdot {2}^{x}+{x}^{3}-{e}^{2}$,  find the slope of the tangent at $x=0.$
question.worked_solution:
Applying the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\cdot {2}^{x}+{x}^{3}-{e}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\cdot {2}^{x})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-{e}^{2}) \\  & =4\cdot {2}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡2+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})+0 \\  & =4\cdot {2}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡2+3{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=0$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=0} & =(4\cdot {2}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡2+3{x}^{2}){|}_{x=0} \\  & =4\cdot {2}^{0}\operatorname{ln}⁡2+3\cdot {0}^{2} \\  & =4\cdot 1\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡2+3\cdot 0 \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$
